name: Scarlet Skips Beginner Guide
description: Watch the rope, make the same small jump, and don’t pile on cards until that jump feels boring.
imageAlt: Scarlet jumping a red and white rope in the park

sections.heading: What Is Scarlet Skips?
paragraphs: Scarlet Skips is a one-button jump-rope game from Yerk Games. [Press, hold and release](/guides/how-to-play) to control [Scarlet](/character). At a level-up, choose one of three [cards](/upgrades) and adjust to what it changes.
More height shifts the landing. Faster or extra ropes change the timing. Later, [Rocket Shoes](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) can extend a jump for [a score route](/guides/high-score).
bullets: Steam, Windows, September 3, 2026.
10 cards. 3 random choices each level.
One Steam achievement. Cards stack.

sections.heading: Basic Controls
paragraphs: There’s one input: press, hold, release. Press just before the rope reaches her feet. Hold only as long as needed, then release with the next pass in mind.
Watch where the rope meets the ground, not [Scarlet](/character)’s hair. That crossing is easier to time repeatedly.
bullets: Let the rope make one full turn before you rush the first jump.
Start with short, repeatable presses instead of holding for maximum height.
When an upgrade changes the timing, spend a few loops learning the new beat.
Use whichever mouse, keyboard or controller binding feels easiest to repeat.

sections.heading: A First-30-Seconds Practice Routine
paragraphs: For the first half-minute, ignore the score. Make the first rope boring. Once a normal jump feels obvious, every card is easier to judge.
bullets: First pass: do nothing and watch where the rope crosses the ground.
Next few passes: use the same short press and notice where Scarlet lands.
Landing too close to the next pass? Release earlier instead of jumping higher.
After the first upgrade, change one thing and give yourself a few loops to adjust.

sections.heading: How Jump Timing Works
paragraphs: The best jump is not always the highest one. You only need enough room to clear the current pattern and land somewhere you can read. Jump too late and the rope catches you; hold too long and you may simply move the mistake to the landing.

[Jump Height](/upgrades/increase-jump-height) and [Rocket Fuel](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) can make a good run feel completely different from its opening. If the old timing suddenly stops working, slow down for a few loops. That does not mean the upgrade was bad.
bullets: Leave enough room to clear the rope without dropping into the next pass.
Hold longer only when the pattern really needs more airtime.
Near the top of the jump, look for the next rope instead of staring at Scarlet.
Treat a new rope or a speed increase as a new rhythm to learn.

sections.heading: How Leveling and Upgrade Choices Work
paragraphs: A level-up pauses the run and gives you three random cards. You cannot force a perfect order, so work with what the game gives you instead of waiting for a checklist to line up. If the name on screen is new, [the card list](/upgrades) is the short answer.
Before you click, ask: what is making this run dangerous right now? Which card helps the goal I actually care about? And can I learn its new timing on the very next loop?
bullets: Pick for this run, not for an imaginary perfect build.
If the next landing already looks bad, take the card that keeps you alive.
Do not chase a combo when neither card fixes the problem in front of you.
If all three choices pull in different directions, [play the pause in a run](/builds#simulator) and watch what actually moves.

sections.heading: Which Upgrades Should Beginners Prioritize?
paragraphs: [Jump Height](/upgrades/increase-jump-height) is the easiest early pick to feel, and [Reinforce Jump Rope](/upgrades/reinforce-jump-rope) is useful when one break would wreck the setup. Players also like [Luck](/upgrades/increase-luck) early, although nobody has published an exact formula for what it changes.

Leave rope speed, extra ropes and fire alone until the current pattern feels comfortable. [Rocket Fuel](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) is much better after a normal jump already stays up for several rope turns.
bullets: Need more breathing room? Take Jump Height, then relearn the landing.
Afraid the setup will collapse? Reinforce the rope before adding more pressure.
Everything feels safe? Luck has more of the run left to help.
Already clearing several turns? Rocket Fuel finally has somewhere useful to take you.

sections.heading: Common Beginner Mistakes
paragraphs: Most early runs go wrong because too many things change at once. When you lose, think back to the first upgrade after which the rhythm felt messy. That choice usually tells you more than the final missed rope.
bullets: Watching Scarlet instead of the rope touching the ground.
Holding every jump as long as possible.
Reacting to one rope at a time instead of watching the whole pattern.
Adding speed, another rope and fire before the new beat feels comfortable.
Copying a [high-score route](/guides/high-score) when you are still trying to survive.

sections.heading: First Build Recommendation
paragraphs: Keep the rope set small, protect it and take height if the landing feels cramped. Add Luck or Rocket Shoes one card at a time once the pattern is comfortable. From there, choose [the ending](/ending), [score](/guides/high-score) or more practice.
bullets: Keep the first plan boring on purpose.
Add one timing change at a time.
Decide whether you want the ending or a score before the late run gets busy.

sections.heading: When Should You Add More Ropes?
paragraphs: Add [another rope](/upgrades/add-jump-rope) only after the current set is protected and one jump can clear several turns. High-score players often wait until the airtime setup is already producing upgrades quickly.
Once the new rope appears, watch a full pattern before you panic-jump. There is usually one repeatable gap where a single jump clears several passes. That gap is what you are looking for.
bullets: An extra rope changes the pattern; it is not free score.
The more ropes you keep, the more [reinforcement](/upgrades/reinforce-jump-rope) matters.
Try to clear a group of passes with one long jump.
For [the ending](/ending), fewer ropes may be easier to control.

sections.heading: Know When the Run Has Changed Shape
paragraphs: At some point a good run stops feeling like normal jump rope. One jump clears lots of turns, upgrades pop while Scarlet is still in the air, and [Rocket Fuel](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) carries you from one choice to the next. When that happens, watch the fuel gauge more than the landing spot — that is the [score route](/guides/high-score) starting to work.
If the run never gets there, it was not wasted. Keep the pattern readable, practice the same input and use it to learn what your next run needs.
bullets: Early run: plan each landing.
Growing run: count how many turns one jump clears and keep the ropes protected.
Airtime run: watch the fuel gauge and how long it takes to reach the next upgrade.
Score run: add speed, more ropes or fire only after the loop works more than once.

seo.title: Scarlet Skips Beginner Guide — Learn the First Jump
seo.description: Learn when to press, hold and release in Scarlet Skips, read the rope at the landing, and choose early cards without losing the timing you just learned.

name: How to Play Scarlet Skips
description: Press, hold, let go. Then three cards. Then the jump changes. Here’s what that loop actually is.
imageAlt: Scarlet missing a skip with the rope tangled around her legs in an official screenshot

sections.heading: Controls
paragraphs: One button. Press to jump, hold to stay up, release to come down. Use whichever mouse, key or controller binding you can repeat comfortably. First rope still a mystery? [Start with the slower guide](/guides/beginner-guide).
Check Settings for the current binding instead of copying a key list from a guide.
bullets: Press to jump.
Hold to stay up.
Release to land.
Later cards change what that same press does.

sections.heading: PC Version and Requirements
paragraphs: Steam lists a Windows version. Price and reviews can change; check the current Steam listing. [Game Info](/game-info) covers controls and system requirements.
bullets: Minimum: Windows 10, Intel i7-6700HQ, 8 GB RAM, GTX 1060, DirectX 12, 2 GB.
Recommended: Ryzen 9 3900X, 16 GB RAM, RTX 2080, DirectX 12, 2 GB.
Single-player. One achievement. Family Sharing.
Yerk Games made it.

sections.heading: Press, Hold and Release
paragraphs: Treat it as one motion, not three commands. The rope says when to press. The pattern says how long to hold. The next ground hit says when to let go.
A short jump is the default. A long hold is for grouped ropes or [Rocket Fuel](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) — not every skip.
bullets: Same short jump until it feels boring.
Hold longer only after height or fuel changes the run.
Let go early enough to see the landing.
Don’t mash once there are extra ropes.

sections.heading: Jump Timing
paragraphs: Watch the rope hit the ground by [Scarlet](/character)’s feet. Jump just before it. At the top, look for the next pass — not her hair.
With extra ropes, don’t chase each strand. Watch one full turn, find the gap, and clear a group with one skip. Still fuzzy? [The first-run guide](/guides/beginner-guide) is slower on purpose.
bullets: Higher is not safer if we land blind.
Speed makes the window smaller.
Extra ropes make a pattern, not a panic.
After a new card, take a few easy skips.

sections.heading: Level Ups
paragraphs: Keep skipping until the game pauses. Three cards. If the name is new, [the card list](/upgrades) has the short answer — including later movement cards the store never lists.
The same card can show up again. That’s stacking. Ask which stack saves this run, not which name sounds strongest.
bullets: The game pauses. We pick one.
Repeats stack.
Don’t wait for a perfect order.
Late airtime runs can get more than one card in a jump.
Safety Bounce is in the files, not in the usual three-card draw.

sections.heading: Upgrade Choices
paragraphs: Pick for the run we have. Height and a shield keep us alive. Luck and fuel grow the run. Extra ropes, speed and fire add pressure. Nobody published the numbers.
Before we click: is this survival, more cards, more air, or more score? If we’re already dying, the plain card that saves the next skip beats a fancy combo.
bullets: Fix what’s about to kill us.
Change one timing thing at a time.
Player orders are not guaranteed best.
Patch 1.0.1 fixed Rocket Shoes and extinguished ropes.

sections.heading: Scoring and Progression
paragraphs: Clean skips raise the counter. Extra ropes, speed, long airtime and fire can make it climb faster. Nobody published the formula.
Someone wrote up ~200,000. Someone else [reached the Moon](/ending). Neither is a leaderboard. Want the counter? [This is the order](/guides/high-score).
bullets: Staying alive is what keeps the number going.
Fire is a multiplier we can see.
Score runs take fire last.
No official global leaderboard.

sections.heading: The Airtime Transition
paragraphs: At some point it stops feeling like jump rope. [Jump Height](/upgrades/increase-jump-height) plus [Rocket Fuel](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) can keep her up long enough for another card. One player says that card refills the tank.
Watch the gauge. Land until the refill happens twice. That’s the [score loop](/guides/high-score).
bullets: Height makes the jump long.
The next card has to arrive before fuel runs out.
Fuel bridges one card to the next.
Then we add ropes, speed or fire.

sections.heading: Losing and Recovering
paragraphs: One miss ends it. Work backward: late jump, held too long, or the last card changed a pattern we never learned?
Next run, change one thing. [The tips page](/guides/tips) is for that first bad pick. [Practice a pause](/builds#simulator) if we just want to see the cards.
bullets: Find the first card that wrecked the rhythm.
Learn that new beat before adding another.
Too many ropes? Shield a smaller set.
Use the run on this site if we just need to see the pause.

sections.heading: Win and Ending Basics
paragraphs: A long run can leave the park. That route grows early, drops extra ropes, shields what’s left, then takes height, Luck and fuel — and skips fire.
[Super Rocket Shoes](/upgrades/super-rocket-shoes) is the late signal. [How we reach the Moon](/ending) hides the ending until we ask for it.
bullets: Moon and score are different routes.
Fewer shielded ropes for the climb.
Nobody published a height number.
Open the ending guide when this run is actually going there.

sections.heading: What the game confirms
paragraphs: The Steam page describes one-button controls, ten upgrade cards, three choices at level-up and stackable cards. It does not publish the scoring formula or a guaranteed best route.
A player route may be useful to try, but it is not a developer rule. Check the linked records below when a specific claim matters to your run.
bullets: Steam page: controls and the advertised card count.
Patch notes: announced changes for that version.
Player reports: routes to try, not guaranteed results.
Unpublished values: do not treat guesses as rules.

seo.title: How to Play Scarlet Skips — Controls and Timing
seo.description: Learn the one-button jump in Scarlet Skips: when to press, how long to hold and what to watch at landing. Then see how three card choices change each run.

name: Scarlet Skips Tips: Fix a Failing Run
description: The opening got messy, the landing went blind, or Rocket Fuel did nothing. Start from the miss and fix that one thing.
imageAlt: Scarlet reacting as rope segments break during a difficult run

sections.heading: Early Run: Protect Information
paragraphs: Open the run with a skip we can repeat. If the first rope still feels random, [make it boring first](/guides/beginner-guide). Change one thing at a time so we can tell what killed the run.
bullets: Take height or a shield if the skip is already tight.
Leave fire and extra ropes alone.
Take Luck only if the landing already feels safe.
After a new card, watch one full rotation before panicking.

sections.heading: Jump Timing: Plan the Descent
paragraphs: Watch the rope hit the ground and plan the landing, not just the launch. A jump can clear this pass and still die because we held into the next one.
bullets: Same short jump, over and over, teaches more than max holds.
Near the top, look for the next rope.
After Jump Height, relearn the landing.
Use [Rocket Fuel](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) on purpose, not as a panic hold.

sections.heading: Upgrade Decisions: Ask Four Questions
paragraphs: There is no best card. On the pause, ask what this run needs before comparing names.
bullets: What’s about to kill us: landing, extra ropes, or slow cards?
Which of these three actually fixes that?
Are we going for the Moon, score, or just surviving?
Can we feel this change on the very next jump?

sections.heading: Rope Management
paragraphs: Every extra rope is another thing to read. More ropes only help when one jump can clear a group of them, and we can still protect what we have.
bullets: Shield a small set before adding another.
Watch the whole pattern, not the nearest strand.
Going for [the Moon](/ending)? Fewer ropes is often better.
Score runs add quantity late, not first.

sections.heading: Airtime and the Refill Test
paragraphs: If the fuel gauge empties before the next card arrives, plan a landing instead of holding on. A player reports a refill when an upgrade appears, but that is not a safety net until we see it work in this run. The [high-score route](/guides/high-score) explains how to build around the loop.
bullets: Watch the gauge when a card appears.
Keep a landing available until a refill repeats.
Later levels can take longer; leave fuel in reserve.

sections.heading: Luck Without an Invented Formula
paragraphs: [Luck](/upgrades/increase-luck) is a reasonable early pick once the jump feels safe. One player guide says it affects how quickly cards appear, but no official percentage is published. Watch what changes in your run instead of trusting a guessed number.
bullets: Earlier Luck has more of the run to work.
Look for LUCKY and cards coming faster.
A quoted cap is not a confirmed rule.
If the next landing is unsafe, take the survival card.

sections.heading: High Score Transition
paragraphs: If the run survives but the score barely moves, check whether another card arrives before fuel runs out. Do not add fire or more ropes to fix a loop that is not working yet. The [high-score guide](/guides/high-score) covers the full card sequence; twelve rope loops is one player's check, not a target we must hit.
bullets: Can the jump reach another card?
Does the fuel refill actually repeat?
If not, keep the pattern readable and land safely.

sections.heading: Ending Transition
paragraphs: If we are aiming for the Moon but extra ropes or fire have made the pattern hard to read, stop following a score build. The [ending route](/ending) explains when to simplify the rope set and which later cards one player used.
bullets: Is this run still for the Moon, or have our picks changed its direction?
Can we protect the ropes we intend to keep?
Treat any quoted height threshold as a player note, not a requirement.

sections.heading: Diagnose a Failed Run
paragraphs: Start from the miss and look for the first card after which the rope became hard to read. If several cards changed the same jump, practice one change at a time next run. Never learned a clean skip? [Start there](/guides/beginner-guide).
bullets: Late jump: watch the ground crossing again.
Bad landing: shorter hold.
Too many ropes: stop adding, shield or drop some.
Cards too slow: consider Luck before more fuel.
Fire wipe: go back to a protected skip.

sections.heading: Claims to Treat Carefully
paragraphs: These guides are young. The ~200,000 run, Luck caps, fuel refills and “twelve loops” are player notes, not developer rules.
bullets: Don’t call a cited score a world record.
Don’t treat a guessed cap as real.
Don’t copy one order as the only order.
After a Rocket Shoes patch, re-test.

seo.title: Scarlet Skips Tips — Fix a Run That Keeps Ending
seo.description: Trace a missed Scarlet Skips jump to its cause: landing timing, extra ropes, speed or a card that changed the rhythm. Try one adjustment on your next run.

name: Off to a Great Start — Scarlet Skips Achievement
description: One Steam achievement. Start a new run, don’t jump, let the first rope hit. That’s it.
imageAlt: Scarlet missing a skip with the rope tangled around her legs

sections.heading: Achievement Facts
paragraphs: Steam lists one achievement, Off to a Great Start, but does not explain its unlock condition. Two player guides say to miss the first jump on purpose. [Game Info](/game-info) has the other store details.
bullets: Achievements listed on Steam: 1.
Name: Off to a Great Start.
Player-reported method: miss the first jump.
The store page does not explain the method.

sections.heading: Before You Start
paragraphs: This has to be a fresh first rope. Skip the intro if we want, but let go before gameplay starts so [Scarlet](/character) doesn’t jump by accident. After it pops, [learn the real jump](/guides/beginner-guide).
bullets: Be online on Steam.
Get through the intro.
Release every jump button before the first rope.
Don’t land a clean skip first.

sections.heading: How to Unlock Off to a Great Start
paragraphs: Two Steam guides say the same thing: fail the first jump. When the first rope comes, do nothing. Let it hit her feet.
bullets: New run.
Hands off mouse, keys and controller.
Let the first rope hit.
Wait for the Steam popup.

sections.heading: What backs this method?
paragraphs: Two separate Steam guides describe the same first-jump miss. That gives the method more support than one report, but it remains player guidance, not a rule published by the developer. After a patch, check [what changed](/updates).
bullets: Steam lists the achievement.
Two player guides describe the miss.
Try it on a fresh run.
A later patch could change it.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: If it doesn’t pop, make the attempt cleaner before assuming the method is wrong. Restart, stay online, and don’t touch anything after the run starts. After a patch, check the [notes](/updates).
bullets: Steam online, notifications on.
Unplug a drifting controller.
Don’t hold the intro-skip into the first rope.
If we already skipped once, start a new run.
Check the version if a patch just dropped.

seo.title: Off to a Great Start — Scarlet Skips Achievement
seo.description: Two player guides report that missing the first jump unlocks Scarlet Skips' listed Steam achievement, Off to a Great Start. See the attempt and evidence.

name: Scarlet Skips High Score Guide
description: Height and Luck first. Rocket Fuel once the jump already hangs. Fire, speed and extra ropes only after we can stay up without them.
imageAlt: Scarlet above a flaming rope with a fire multiplier

sections.heading: The pick order
paragraphs: This is the score route on [Builds](/builds#score). Early cards look like a Moon climb. Then we split: fire and extra ropes belong here, not on [the way to the Moon](/ending).
Someone wrote up a run around 200,000. Useful as a picture of the loop. Not a record, not a formula.
bullets: Jump Height and Luck first.
Rocket Fuel once a normal jump already hangs.
More ropes and speed after that loop repeats.
Fire last, when losing a rope is easy.

sections.heading: Early run: make room for a long jump
paragraphs: Take [Jump Height](/upgrades/increase-jump-height) and [Luck](/upgrades/increase-luck) once the skip is readable. Stay around two to four ropes and [shield](/upgrades/reinforce-jump-rope) what we have.
Leave [Ignite](/upgrades/ignite-jump-rope) alone. Fire looks like score. Early fire is usually a shorter run.
bullets: Keep the pattern small enough to read.
Shield before adding another rope.
Fuel does nothing if the jump still can’t spend it.

sections.heading: Mid run: make the fuel loop repeat
paragraphs: Add [Rocket Fuel](/upgrades/upgrade-rocket-fuel) after height is already doing work. We want several rope passes — and later another card — inside one jump.

A player says a new card refills the tank. Watch the gauge when it resolves. Make that happen twice before we bet the run on it. First rope still random? [Learn the jump](/guides/beginner-guide) first.
bullets: Height makes the jump long.
Luck is how the next card shows up in the air.
Fuel bridges one card to the next.
Land until the refill happens twice.

sections.heading: Late run: turn spare safety into score
paragraphs: When cards start arriving before we land, add ropes and [speed](/upgrades/increase-jump-rope-speed). Take fire only if a broken rope is easy to replace.
Later levels take longer. Leave more fuel in the tank. The [tips page](/guides/tips) is the short version of this.
bullets: More ropes after we can already stay up.
Speed one step at a time.
Fire multiplies the counter. It is not the engine.
Keep taking fuel as the gaps get longer.

sections.heading: Signs the engine is ready
paragraphs: Don’t wait for a magic number. One write-up used about twelve loops in a jump as a personal check. What matters to this route is whether the next card arrives before the fuel gauge empties.
bullets: One jump clears several passes.
Cards start showing up in the air.
The gauge actually refills.
We can do that bridge twice.

sections.heading: What usually ruins a score attempt
paragraphs: Copying this order on a Moon run is how a clean skip turns into a miss. If we want the ending, that’s [a different route](/builds#moon).
bullets: Fire too early.
Extra ropes before they’re shielded.
Fuel without enough height.
Holding until the tank is empty.
Treating ~200,000 as a world record.

seo.title: Scarlet Skips High Score Guide — Build the Airtime Loop
seo.description: Try a player-reported Scarlet Skips score route: build height and Luck, test whether Rocket Shoes keeps you airborne, then add ropes and fire if the loop holds.

name: Scarlet Skips Spectacle Guide
description: Extra ropes, fire, speed and tricks. This is the store-shot run — not the one that reaches the Moon.
imageAlt: A jump rope breaking into segments during a busy run

sections.heading: What this route is for
paragraphs: This is the loud route on [Builds](/builds#spectacle). Extra ropes, fire, speed, bounce, air tricks. That’s the look the store sells. A Moon climb wants the opposite.
Score uses some of the same late cards. Difference is intent. Here we take the loud pick even when the quiet one would score more.
bullets: Fire and extra ropes are the look.
Bounce, air tricks and charge are extras, not the engine.
Don’t use this order if we actually want [the Moon](/ending).

sections.heading: Do not start loud
paragraphs: We still need a jump we can read. Take [Jump Height](/upgrades/increase-jump-height) and [Reinforce](/upgrades/reinforce-jump-rope) before crowding the park. First rope still a mystery? [Start there](/guides/beginner-guide).
An extra rope is not free spectacle. It changes the whole pattern.
bullets: Height and a shield first.
Shield new ropes.
Don’t take rope count and speed back to back.

sections.heading: Add ropes when the gap is readable
paragraphs: Take [Add Jump Rope](/upgrades/add-jump-rope) once several passes fit in one jump. Watch a full rotation before panicking. There’s usually one gap where a single skip clears several.
If shields fall behind, take protection over another rope. Quantity without shields is how it falls apart.
bullets: Read the whole spacing, not the nearest strand.
Protect or replace losses before adding another.
If the gap disappears, stop scaling.

sections.heading: Fire is the look
paragraphs: [Ignite](/upgrades/ignite-jump-rope) is why this run looks like the store. Official shots show a fire multiplier. Score routing still puts fire last, because a burning unprotected rope is a short show.
Take it when losing a rope is easy. Stop adding fire when we can’t see the gap anymore.
bullets: Fire after we can still read the pattern.
Keep a shield available.
Extinguish undoes a rope that got too hot.

sections.heading: Speed and tricks
paragraphs: [Rope Speed](/upgrades/increase-jump-rope-speed) makes the same pattern harder. [Bounce](/upgrades/bounce-tricks), [Air Tricks](/upgrades/air-tricks) and [Charge Jump](/upgrades/charge-jump) change how a skip feels. They’re extras, not a replacement for height.
Change one at a time. Two rhythm cards in a row is how we lose the gap we just learned.
bullets: Speed one step at a time.
Tricks after the ropes are already a show.
If the landing goes blind, stop adding stuff.

sections.heading: This is not the Moon
paragraphs: The Moon route uses fewer ropes and skips fire. If Super Rocket Shoes is the point, switch on [Builds](/builds#moon) and read [how we get there](/ending).
If we still want the counter more than the mess, the [score guide](/guides/high-score) delays the same loud cards until the fuel loop repeats.
bullets: Moon: fewer ropes, no fire.
Score: same loud cards, later.
Spectacle: take the loud pick on purpose.

seo.title: Scarlet Skips Spectacle Guide — Ropes, Fire and Tricks
seo.description: Build a busy Scarlet Skips run with extra ropes, fire, speed and trick cards. Learn how to keep the pattern readable and why this is not the Moon route.
